units.source_text: 我把母亲叫到一边，悄悄询问父亲的病情。

en.t: I called my mother aside and quietly asked about my father's illness.

units.source_text: “我爸到院子里干这干那的，也不歇着，身子吃得消吗？”

en.t: Does my father have the strength to keep going around the yard doing this and that without even resting?

units.source_text: “他已经不觉得哪儿难受啦，大概是好了吧。”

en.t: He does not feel any pain or discomfort anymore. I suppose he must be better.

units.source_text: 没想到母亲很不以为然，

en.t: To my surprise, my mother took it quite lightly,

units.source_text: 和那些生活在远离都市的森林里或乡间的农妇一样，母亲对这类事情完全是无知的。

en.t: Like peasant women living in forests or the countryside far from the city, my mother was completely ignorant about such matters.

units.source_text: 但是，上次父亲晕倒的时候，她又是那么惊慌，那么担心。

en.t: And yet, when my father had collapsed the last time, she had been so frightened and so worried.

units.source_text: 我心里忽然产生一种奇妙的感觉。

en.t: A strange feeling suddenly arose in me.

units.source_text: “可是，当时医生不是已经发话，很难好利索了吗？”

en.t: But didn't the doctor say at the time that it would be very hard for him to make a full recovery?

units.source_text: “所以说嘛，没有比人的身体更奇怪的了。

en.t: That is just what I mean; there is nothing stranger than the human body.

units.source_text: 你看看，医生说得那么严重，可现在你爸不是还挺精神的嘛。

en.t: Look, the doctor made it sound so serious, and yet your father is still quite lively now.

units.source_text: 起初，我也很担心，尽量不让他下地。

en.t: At first I was worried too, and tried as much as I could not to let him get up and move around.

units.source_text: 唉，你爸的脾气你也知道的，调养倒也调养，就是倔得要命。

en.t: Well, you know your father's temperament; he does take care of himself, but he is terribly stubborn.

units.source_text: 自己觉得已经好了的话，根本听不进我的话。”

en.t: Once he decides he is already better, he simply will not listen to me.
